Messages.Author: JoshtheNOS
Messages.Body: ok, i am a new to the game and cant seem to find this in the rulebook. What all can i include in my crypt. What i am getting at is what all types of vampires can i include in one crypt.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body: Only restrictions are that they must be from two consecutive vampire groups, like for example groups 3 and 4 (having all from same group is just fine too).

Messages.Author: Mephistopheles
Messages.Body:
And just be 100% sure you don't miss this: you must have at least 12 crypt cards, but there is no upper limit. I know you didn't ask for this, but maybe I helped with this.

Messages.Author: Wookie813
Messages.Body:
...and while you can include whichever vampires you want in your crypt (within the restriction of them all being from no more than 2 consecutive groupings), common strategy is to include vampires who share a discipline or two to utilize discipline based cards in your crypt, or vampires of the same clan to facilitate certain clan cards (and often a combination of both strategies).

I suggest a new strategy...let the Wookie win.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
So far, there is one crypt card that can be used in any crypt, that's the Anarch Convert. His grouping is "ANY".

Also, even though some players wish it, groupings 1 and 6 are not consecutive (it doesn't close on itself).

Messages.Author: DeathInABottle
Messages.Body:
> JoshtheNOS wrote:
> What are the groupings?
>
Look at the bottom left, below the picture: you'll see a number between 1 and 6, or nothing at all. If there's a number, that's the group. If there's no number, the card was released before the grouping rules came into effect, and it means it's either group 1 or 2: if there's no symbol in the top right, it's group 1 (released during the original Jyhad/VTES era); if there's an expansion symbol, it's group 2.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
Let me recommend you try building decks with ARDB (or just put a copy of them there). It has a few useful functions, one of them being that it highlights illegal crypt-combinations by making the suspect vampires red in the list.

If you have an idea for a deck, put it on here and throw up a bunch of "I'm a Newbie" caveats so that you get the kind of advice you need. The Deck Clinic is that place for all of that sort of thing.
